projects.title: MetaExtract
projects.tagline: Large modular extraction system for heterogeneous document workflows
projects.proofSummary: Shows deep modular extraction architecture with reliability-focused workflow design.
projects.demonstrates: How I design modular extraction systems that handle real document variability while staying operable for teams.
projects.description: A large modular extraction system for parsing PDFs, images, and document variations in document-heavy operations. Built for reliable extraction under noisy, inconsistent, real-world inputs.
projects.problem: Organizations need to extract structured metadata from thousands of heterogeneous documents — invoices, contracts, medical records, research papers — each with different formats and field layouts.
projects.approach: Built a FastAPI backend with a modular extraction pipeline. Each document type gets a dedicated parser combining regex patterns, layout analysis, and ML classification. Results are normalized into a unified schema and served via REST API with React dashboard for monitoring.
projects.result: Large modular extraction system built for document-heavy healthcare workflows.

technicalDepth.architecture: Modular FastAPI backend with pluggable parsers per document type. Async job queue for batch processing. PostgreSQL for metadata storage, Redis for caching.
technicalDepth.ocrPipeline: Tesseract OCR with custom preprocessing (deskewing, denoising, contrast normalization). Layout analysis using heuristic + ML-based region detection.
technicalDepth.normalization: Unified schema mapping variations to standardized outputs. Confidence scoring per field with fallback rules.
technicalDepth.performance: Handles 1000+ pages/hour on single instance. Sub-2s response for single-page documents.
technicalDepth.integration: REST API with webhook callbacks. React dashboard for monitoring queue status and reviewing extraction accuracy.

outcomes: Processing highly variable semantic structures from heterogeneous document formats
Reduced manual data entry by ~80% for healthcare document workflows
Confidence scoring enables human review queue prioritization
Deployed in production handling thousands of documents weekly
projects.ownership: Owned system design and implementation end-to-end: extraction pipeline, normalization logic, API layer, and operator-facing monitoring flow.
constraints: Heterogeneous source documents with inconsistent layouts and noisy scans
Need for usable confidence scores to support human review queues
Production reliability requirements in document-heavy healthcare operations
tradeoffs: Used a hybrid rules + ML approach instead of model-only extraction to keep outputs debuggable and reliable by field type
Prioritized high-confidence core fields first, then expanded long-tail field coverage incrementally
whatChanged: Manual extraction and copy-paste became API-backed structured outputs
Review teams moved from full-document checking to confidence-prioritized exception review
artifacts: Queue-level extraction status view for operations
Per-field confidence and normalization trace for reviewer decisions
Unified output schema mapping thousands of field variants

projects.title: CodeCollector
projects.tagline: Codebase analysis CLI — zero-config pattern detection and complexity reports
projects.description: A command-line tool that scans codebases, extracts patterns, and generates structured analysis reports. Built for developers who need quick insights into code quality and architecture.
projects.problem: Developers joining new projects or auditing existing codebases need quick, structured insights without setting up heavy analysis tools or IDEs.
projects.approach: Built as a Python CLI using AST parsing and pattern matching. Generates JSON/Markdown reports with metrics on code complexity, duplication, dependency graphs, and anti-pattern detection. Designed for zero-config usage with sensible defaults.
projects.result: Python CLI using AST parsing for codebase pattern detection and complexity reports.

projects.title: Caption Art
projects.tagline: AI-powered creative automation for visual content
projects.description: An AI creative tool that generates artistic captions, applies style transfers, and creates visual content using generative AI models. Combines text generation with image manipulation.
projects.problem: Content creators and social media managers spend hours crafting captions and visual styles for each post. Existing tools are either too generic or require design skills.
projects.approach: React + TypeScript frontend with FastAPI backend. Integrated Fal AI for generative models. Users upload images, select style parameters, and the system generates styled captions and visual variations. Pipeline includes image analysis, style matching, and text generation.
projects.result: Generative AI pipeline combining image analysis, style matching, and text generation via Fal AI.

projects.title: SignKit
projects.tagline: Signature extraction & PDF signing — commercial desktop product
projects.proofSummary: Shows ability to package workflow software into a paid product with trust-critical surfaces.
projects.demonstrates: How I take a workflow pain point from idea to paid product with real usage and operational constraints.
projects.description: A commercial desktop application for signature extraction and PDF document processing. PySide6 frontend with FastAPI backend, PostgreSQL database, and PDF signing capabilities. Handles batch document workflows for legal and financial teams. Built from idea to paid product.
projects.problem: Legal and financial teams process thousands of signed documents daily. They need signature extraction, PDF signing, and organized output management in one complete workflow.
projects.approach: PySide6 cross-platform desktop app with FastAPI backend. PostgreSQL for document metadata and user management. OpenCV-based signature extraction with morphological operations. PDF signing with embedded certificate support.
projects.result: Paid product with early customer validation — signature extraction, PDF signing, and billing shipped end-to-end.

technicalDepth.cvPipeline: OpenCV morphological operations (dilation, erosion, contour detection) to isolate signature regions. Handles handwritten signatures on scanned documents, photos, and mixed backgrounds.
technicalDepth.backend: FastAPI with async document processing. PostgreSQL for user accounts, document metadata, and audit trails. File storage with organized output folders.
technicalDepth.signing: PDF signing with embedded certificate chains. Signature appearance customization. Batch signing for multi-document workflows.
technicalDepth.monetization: Stripe integration for subscription billing. License key validation. Trial mode with full feature access for 14 days.
technicalDepth.distribution: Cross-platform builds for Windows and macOS. Code-signed binaries. Auto-updater integration.

outcomes: Paid product with early customer validation
Signature extraction accuracy >90% on clean documents, >75% on degraded scans
Batch processing workflows save legal teams hours per week
projects.ownership: Owned product and build from idea to paid release: desktop UX, extraction/signing pipeline, billing integration, packaging, and shipping workflow.
constraints: Needed both signature extraction and signing in one operational flow, not separate tools
Cross-platform distribution and update reliability for non-technical end users
Accuracy requirements on imperfect scanned documents
tradeoffs: Chose desktop-first workflow (PySide6) for local file-heavy operations instead of web-only upload flow
Focused initial release on core extraction + signing reliability before broader template and collaboration features
whatChanged: Replaced fragmented manual signing process with a single structured workflow
Moved from prototype utility to paid product with licensing and subscription flow
artifacts: Batch signing queue with status tracking
Signature region extraction pipeline and confidence checks

projects.title: EchoPanel
projects.tagline: Local-first meeting intelligence — capture, transcribe, search, and retrieve
projects.proofRole: Platform breadth + real product use case
projects.proofSummary: Shows product workflow thinking across capture, processing, retrieval, and usable operational UI.
projects.demonstrates: How I combine product workflow design with technical implementation to build practical local-first systems.
projects.description: A native macOS workflow system that captures meeting audio, transcribes in near real time, and makes transcript retrieval actually usable in day-to-day work.
projects.problem: Professionals in meetings, interviews, and research need to capture and search audio content without switching between multiple tools or relying on cloud services.
projects.approach: Swift menu bar app using AVFoundation for audio capture. FastAPI backend with Whisper for transcription. SQLite for local transcript storage with full-text search. Designed for minimal UI presence with maximum utility.
projects.result: Local-first meeting intelligence prototype combining native UX, transcript retrieval, and practical workflow value.

technicalDepth.audioCapture: AVFoundation audio engine with custom audio buffer management. Captures system audio via CoreAudio APIs. Real-time streaming to backend.
technicalDepth.transcription: Whisper model (base/large) for on-device transcription. Chunked processing for real-time results. Speaker diarization experiments.
technicalDepth.storage: SQLite with FTS5 for full-text search. Local-first architecture with export options (SRT, TXT, JSON).
technicalDepth.ux: Menu bar widget with global hotkey. Minimal UI: record button, status indicator, transcript view. Searchable history with timestamp navigation.
technicalDepth.integration: FastAPI backend for optional cloud processing. WebSocket streaming for live transcription preview.

outcomes: Native macOS UX with global hotkey activation
Real-time transcription with Whisper on Apple Silicon
Local-first storage with full-text search across transcripts
Export formats: SRT, plain text, structured JSON
projects.ownership: Owned prototype architecture and implementation across native app layer, transcription pipeline integration, and local-first transcript retrieval flow.
constraints: Needed low-friction capture from a menu bar workflow, not a heavy standalone app
Latency had to stay acceptable for near-real-time transcript feedback
Local-first storage and search expectations for privacy-sensitive usage
tradeoffs: Prioritized reliable capture + searchable transcript history over broad collaboration features
Used practical chunked processing strategy to balance speed and accuracy during live sessions
whatChanged: Audio capture and transcript retrieval moved from ad-hoc tools to one integrated flow
Users could search transcript history by content and timestamp instead of replaying long recordings
artifacts: Menu bar recorder with status and quick actions

projects.title: EchoAI-MLX
projects.tagline: Fine-tuned Whisper on Apple Silicon
projects.description: Fine-tuned Whisper speech recognition model optimized for Apple Silicon using the MLX framework. Demonstrates on-device ML training and inference.
projects.problem: Cloud-based speech recognition has latency, privacy, and cost issues. On-device models need optimization for specific hardware and use cases.
projects.approach: Used Apple's MLX framework to fine-tune Whisper on domain-specific audio data. Optimized for Apple Silicon GPU and Neural Engine. Benchmarking against base Whisper models for accuracy and speed.
projects.result: Fine-tuned Whisper on Apple Silicon using MLX. Benchmarked against base models for accuracy and speed on domain-specific audio.

projects.title: PhotoSearch
projects.tagline: Local-first natural language media search and analysis workstation
projects.proofSummary: Shows multimodal retrieval product design with local-first workflow constraints.
projects.demonstrates: How I build local-first multimodal products where natural language retrieval, clustering, and review workflows work together.
projects.description: A local-first media search and analysis workstation using natural language retrieval, metadata exploration, and people clustering as one layer of a broader workflow.
projects.problem: Large local media libraries become hard to search and review with folders and filenames alone. Teams need natural language retrieval, metadata visibility, and review workflows that feel like a workstation.
projects.approach: Built a FastAPI + LanceDB backend with CLIP-based semantic retrieval, local-first indexing, and Tauri desktop workflows. Added people clustering as a supporting layer, not the primary product story.
projects.result: Local-first media search workstation with natural language retrieval, metadata workflows, and multimodal analysis.

technicalDepth.architecture: FastAPI service layer with separate indexing and query paths. LanceDB stores embeddings; desktop client uses Tauri + React for local workflow UX.
technicalDepth.performance: Incremental indexing for large libraries and sub-second retrieval on common semantic query paths after warm cache.
technicalDepth.integration: Combined CLIP semantic retrieval with person clustering and metadata workflows to support concept, context, and identity-oriented review paths.

outcomes: Semantic retrieval over 10K+ photo libraries with practical interactive latency
Face clustering reduced manual album organization overhead
Desktop workflow unified indexing, query, and review in one tool
projects.ownership: Owned full-stack implementation of indexing, natural-language retrieval, metadata flows, and desktop workflow orchestration.
constraints: Large local libraries with mixed quality metadata and inconsistent naming
Need for a desktop-first experience that can handle long indexing runs
Balancing semantic relevance, people clustering quality, and query latency
tradeoffs: Prioritized local workstation workflow and retrieval quality over cloud sync features in early versions
Shipped semantic retrieval + clustering workflow before broader media management capabilities
whatChanged: Browsing by folders and filenames shifted to concept-driven retrieval
People-centric queries became practical via face clustering instead of manual tagging
artifacts: Indexing status workflow for large photo libraries
Semantic query interface with ranked result grid
Face cluster review and merge flow

projects.title: model-lab
projects.tagline: Audio pipeline evaluation workbench for ASR/diarization reliability testing
projects.proofSummary: Shows repeatable model-comparison discipline and reliability-focused pipeline evaluation.
projects.description: A systematic audio pipeline evaluation workbench for ASR, diarization, and related model workflows. Built for repeatable comparisons across quality, speed, cost, and hardware constraints.
projects.problem: Selecting the right audio AI model requires systematic evaluation across accuracy, speed, cost, and hardware — not just running a few tests. Teams need infrastructure to make deployment decisions with data.
projects.approach: Built model-lab as a repeatable evaluation framework with shared harness, identical metrics, and automated comparison dashboards. Tested across Apple Silicon MPS, NVIDIA CUDA, and CPU. Produced production readiness grades for Whisper variants and LFM2.5-Audio.
projects.result: Evaluation harness for ASR pipeline comparison with repeatable runs, scorecards, and hardware-aware findings.

Community-driven disposal facility database.

faq.question: What's the smallest scope you've taken?
faq.answer: The smallest was a two-week document extraction prototype for a healthcare startup that needed to validate before their board meeting. They had a vague brief, I scoped it, built it, and they used the results to justify a full build. If the problem is clear and the scope is real, I'll take it on.

faq.question: What if I only have a vague idea?
faq.answer: That's fine. Most good engagements start with 'we have this problem and we think AI might help.' I ask a lot of questions in the discovery call to get to the actual problem — not the stated solution. If the fit isn't there, I'll tell you.

faq.question: Do you work with existing teams?
faq.answer: Yes. I've augmented teams for specific sprints and projects. I'm comfortable working in your codebase, your workflow, and your stack — as long as the problem is well-defined.

faq.question: What does a typical week look like?
faq.answer: Week 1 is discovery and scoping. Week 2 onwards, you get a working demo every Friday. You see code, you see the system working, you can interact with it. Not a slide deck, not a status report.

faq.question: Do you handle deployment and DevOps?
faq.answer: Yes. Docker containers, AWS deployments, CI/CD pipelines, and monitoring are included in prototype and automation engagements. I don't hand off 'call someone else to deploy.'
